title: Resolving vectors into perpendicular components practice

question_set_contract.difficulty_progression: direct Lesson 10 retrieval, basic angle recognition, angle measured from vertical, component meaning, two complete resolutions, then a mixed resolution-and-addition route

evidence_basis.originality_note: All wording, contexts, values and planned diagrams are newly authored. The mapped P2 leaves ground perpendicular projection, angle-reference choice, signed components and component-based resultants, while their later-topic laws are excluded.

questions.prompt: From Lesson 10, describe how to add vector A to vector B using a head-to-tail diagram and state how the resultant is drawn.
A vector has magnitude 10 N and is directed at $30^\circ$ above the positive horizontal axis. What is its horizontal component?
A 20 m vector is directed $40^\circ$ east of north. Which expressions give its east and north component magnitudes?
Which statement about two perpendicular components of one vector is correct?

options.A: Their vector sum equals the original vector, and their values depend on the chosen perpendicular axes.
options.B: Their magnitudes must add arithmetically to the magnitude of the original vector.
options.C: Each component must have the same magnitude as the original vector.
options.D: Sine always gives the horizontal component and cosine always gives the vertical component.

questions.prompt: A pull vector has magnitude 46 N and is directed $28^\circ$ above the horizontal towards the right.

figure.purpose: Provide the stated vector and perpendicular axes while leaving both component arrows and all calculations for the learner.
figure.brief: Original Cambridge-inspired black-and-white rectangular line diagram. Show horizontal and vertical axes through an origin and one 46 N arrow at 28 degrees above the positive horizontal. Label only 46 N and 28 degrees. Leave space for the learner to draw and label the two components. Do not draw projection lines, component arrows or answer values.
figure.alt_text: A 46 newton vector points 28 degrees above a horizontal axis.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: On the figure, draw and label the horizontal and vertical components of the vector.

questions.prompt: A displacement vector has magnitude 72 m and is directed $58^\circ$ south of west.

figure.purpose: Make the southwest direction and angle reference unambiguous while requiring the learner to construct and calculate both directed components.
figure.brief: Original Cambridge-inspired black-and-white rectangular vector diagram. Show north-east compass axes through an origin and a 72 m arrow into the southwest quadrant. Mark 58 degrees between the arrow and the west direction. Leave the component triangle, arrows, labels and values blank.
figure.alt_text: A 72 metre vector points 58 degrees south of west on compass axes.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: On the figure, draw and label the westward and southward components.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Calculate the magnitude of the westward component.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Calculate the magnitude of the southward component.

questions.prompt: A survey marker is moved by vector A, which has magnitude 30 m at $40^\circ$ north of east. It is then moved by vector B, which is 12 m west.

figure.purpose: Support a mixed current-and-prior vector route by fixing directions while leaving resolution, signed addition and the final resultant learner-generated.
figure.brief: Original Cambridge-inspired black-and-white rectangular diagram. Show east-north axes and vector A as a 30 m arrow 40 degrees north of east from the origin. Separately show vector B as a 12 m west arrow with no head-to-tail placement. Leave all component arrows, signed totals, resultant and final angle blank.
figure.alt_text: Vector A is 30 metres at 40 degrees north of east, and vector B is 12 metres west.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Resolve vector A into eastward and northward components.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Using Lesson 10 vector addition, determine the final eastward and northward components after vector B is added.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Calculate the magnitude of the resultant displacement.

parts.label: (d)
parts.prompt: Calculate the direction of the resultant displacement, measured north of east.
